title: The Case for Christ: A Journalist's Personal Investigation of the Evidence for Jesus
author: Lee Strobel
edition_analyzed: Original edition (later updated and expanded editions available)
target_audience: Skeptics and seekers curious about Christianity
Christians seeking to strengthen their faith
Readers interested in historical analysis of Jesus
Those exploring religious and spiritual questions
core_themes: Historical reliability of the Christian Gospels
Existence, identity, and resurrection of Jesus
Application of journalistic and legal standards to religious claims
Personal transformation through examination of evidence
primary_purpose: To investigate the historical and factual validity of key Christian claims about Jesus using journalistic methods, presenting evidence to support Christianity and address common doubts.

structure_format.organization: Divided into interviews with leading scholars, organized around major issues (evidence for Jesus’ existence, deity, crucifixion, and resurrection)
features: Q&A interviews with experts in theology, history, medicine, and textual criticism

key_concepts_lessons: Eyewitness evidence, manuscript reliability, and archaeological support for the Gospels
Historical arguments for Jesus’ death, burial, and resurrection
Criteria for evaluating ancient documents and testimonies
The cumulative case approach strengthens arguments for the historicity of Jesus
Skepticism can be addressed with historically and logically grounded responses
notable_features: Includes interviews with prominent scholars from various relevant fields
Addresses key objections to Christian claims
Offers a narrative of personal faith journey alongside investigative findings
Supplemented by readers’ guides and adaptations for youth
cultural_historical_context: Published in the late 1990s, amid growing cultural interest in religious skepticism and the historicity of Jesus. The book offered a fresh, journalistic approach to apologetics targeting a modern audience raised on evidential and courtroom reasoning.
reception_impact: Widely popular among evangelical Christians and seekers; over 5 million copies sold
Frequently used in small groups, outreach, and educational settings
Praised for accessible style and comprehensive approach to evidence
Criticized by some scholars for selection bias and for interviewing primarily evangelical experts
Adapted into a film and children’s/youth versions
comparable_titles: Evidence That Demands a Verdict by Josh McDowell
Cold-Case Christianity by J. Warner Wallace
The Case for Faith (also by Lee Strobel)
